INTEGRATION STEP for Product Oracle v1. Read docs/v1-plan.md in full first. Lanes A (members), B2a/B2b (connectors) are already on main. The other lanes' work is on branches of origin: lane/k-connections, lane/b1-sources, lane/c-baseline, lane/f-templates, lane/d1-mcp, lane/d2-mcp-oauth, lane/e-runs (fetch them with git fetch origin 'refs/heads/lane/*:refs/remotes/origin/lane/*'). Each was built in parallel from an older main, and none was tested together.

1. Merge them into this branch in this order: k-connections, b1-sources, c-baseline, f-templates, d1-mcp, d2-mcp-oauth, e-runs. Resolve every conflict by keeping both lanes' intent: route registration in api/oracle/main.py, the generated web/lib/api (regenerate with `make openapi`, never hand-merge it), shared web navigation and components, and any duplicated helpers (B1 and K both read connection credentials: keep K's connections.service.get_credential and make B1 call it). Migrations: 0001-0003 on main, 0004 from d2-mcp-oauth; there must be one linear chain.
2. Wire the lanes together where each one left a hook: register D2's OAuth access-token verifier with D1's oracle.mcp.auth registry; make D1's curated search tool return B1's confidence; make E's runs ingest a segment's baseline.yaml artifact through C's YAML import (locks respected, proposals created); make F's priorities read C's evidence confidence.
3. Run everything: the full API suite against Postgres (ORACLE_TEST_DATABASE_URL), ruff check and ruff format --check, `make openapi` (commit the result), web lint, tsc, build, the Playwright mock suite, and `make e2e` if Postgres and Chromium are available. Fix what fails. If Chromium cannot start here, say so plainly; CI runs it.
4. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/integrate-report.md: conflicts and how each was resolved, wiring done, test results with counts, anything not verified.
Product Oracle words only: one company's Oracle, its users and their roles; never 'workspace'. Never touch .github/. Commit your work.

CLAUDE ACCOUNT POOL for Product Oracle v1, with EXACTLY SwarmCloud's account management (owner's instruction: 'use the EXACT account management functionality as in SwarmCloud; the app is used locally, for experimentation, for local personal use'). Read docs/v1-plan.md section 'Claude accounts' and docs/questions.md row P3b first. Then read SwarmCloud's public repo (git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud into a scratch directory outside this checkout, read only): apps/quota-broker/quota_broker/ (accounts.py, accountstore.py, oauth.py, credentials.py, usage.py, usagepoll.py, main.py account routes), apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/accountlease.py and runners/cliagent.py (rate_limit_event readings, swap at a turn boundary), apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/routes/accounts.py, apps/swarm-ui/src/Accounts.tsx, apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/sc.py and render.py, docs/account-holders.md and docs/quota-management.md. Port that behaviour into Oracle exactly: data model fields, label rule, states and state_before_reauth, quota windows, holds with TTL and a hold log, the browser sign-in (authorize URL, PKCE, pasted code#state, owner check, token exchange with the same request shape and headers), the paste route for Claude Code's saved login JSON (refresh token required), the single-writer refresh sweep with its timings, hold deferral and write order, reauth detection and recovery, usage polling limits and readings merge, staleness, the assignment policy and its no-account reasons, swap and drain, pause/resume/drain/remove, the API routes (owner-only changes), the accounts screen (rows, tiles, holders and history tabs, owner actions, remove by typing the label, the em dash and ~ marks, CLEARS) and the CLI (oracle account add|pause|resume|drain|remove, oracle accounts with the same columns and footnote). Copy the logic; do not import or call SwarmCloud at runtime. Adapt only these: no lending (one company); credentials encrypted in Oracle's database with oracle.crypto instead of Secret Manager; the sweep runs from `oracle tick` and a local background scheduler instead of Cloud Scheduler; Firestore documents become Postgres tables via migration 0005 (down_revision 0004) with tenant scoping; a setup-token or Anthropic API key is the fallback credential used when no account is registered, as SwarmCloud's tenant secret is. Oracle's calls run through Claude Code headless (claude-agent-sdk or `claude -p --output-format stream-json`) with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set for that call only. This replaces the per-user Claude plan in api/oracle/llm/ and its card on Settings > Connections; data connections stay per user and untouched. UI: Settings > Claude accounts. Tests mirroring SwarmCloud's for choice, states, drain, refresh order and deferral, reauth, readings merge, usage poll limits, display marks, plus role checks and a Playwright mock test. Run the full API suite, ruff, make openapi, web lint/tsc/build, Playwright mock tests. Commit. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/claude-accounts-report.md listing every SwarmCloud file you ported from and every adaptation. Product Oracle words only for everything else (users, roles; never 'workspace'); never touch .github/.
